answers.reset_flush: The always_ff process at line 154 is sensitive to posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni. A low rst_ni asynchronously clears q at line 158; with reset deasserted, flush_i clears q on the next rising clock edge at lines 162 and 165, taking priority over the next-count update at line 171. n is not directly reset or flushed; it is combinationally calculated from q and the inputs.

count_behavior.definitions: With reset deasserted and no flush, full_o=(q==8), empty_o=(q==0). A push is accepted when push_i && !full_o (line 99); a pop is accepted when pop_i && !empty_o (line 119). The next value is captured in q at the next rising clock edge.
count_behavior.push_only: An accepted push sets n=q+1 (line 116); when full, the push is blocked and n=q.
count_behavior.pop_only: An accepted pop sets n=q-1 (line 127); when empty, the pop is blocked and n=q.
count_behavior.both: When 0<q<8 both are accepted and the final assignment at line 131 sets n=q. At q=0 only the push is accepted, yielding n=1; at q=8 only the pop is accepted, yielding n=7. These boundary cases violate the corresponding source assertions and can terminate simulation; the stated values describe the RTL combinational assignments if execution proceeds.
count_behavior.neither: n=q by the default assignment at line 79, so q holds on the next clock edge.

answers.read_modify_write: There is no in-place source assignment to q in the increment or decrement: the combinational assignments read q and write the distinct variable n at lines 116 and 127. The separate clocked nonblocking assignment q<=n at line 171 later commits the selected next value. Thus the counter has feedback across n/q staging, but neither arithmetic statement is an in-place read_write access to q.
